title: Java Medium Level Assessment
subject: Java Programming
target: Mid-level Java developers with 2-4 years of experience. Covers core Java, OOP, concurrency, collections, streams, and design patterns.

questionList.title: OOP: Method Overriding vs Overloading
options: display(int) in Child is overriding, display(String) in Child is overloading
Both display(int) and display(String) are overriding
display(int) is overloading, display(String) is overriding
Neither is overriding because Parent only has one method
questionList.answer: display(int) in Child is overriding, display(String) in Child is overloading

questionList.title: HashMap Hash Collision
options: Outputs 1 — HashMap uses equals() to distinguish keys in the same bucket
Outputs 2 — second put overwrites the first
Runtime exception due to hash collision
Outputs null — HashMap rejects duplicate hashes
questionList.answer: Outputs 1 — HashMap uses equals() to distinguish keys in the same bucket

questionList.title: Finally Block with Return
options: 3 — finally block's return overrides the try block's return
1 — try block returns before finally executes
2 — since no exception, catch is skipped
Compilation error
questionList.answer: 3 — finally block's return overrides the try block's return

questionList.title: volatile Keyword Guarantee
options: Visibility — changes by one thread are immediately visible to all threads
Atomicity — the flag = true operation is atomic
Both visibility and mutual exclusion like synchronized
Only prevents CPU-level caching
questionList.answer: Visibility — changes by one thread are immediately visible to all threads

questionList.title: String Pool and == Operator

questionList.title: equals() and hashCode() Contract
options: hashCode() must be overridden when equals() is overridden, or HashMap/HashSet will behave incorrectly

equals() alone is sufficient for all collection types

questionList.title: Synchronized: Static vs Instance

methodA blocks methodB because static takes precedence

questionList.answer: They can run concurrently — static locks on Class object, instance locks on this

questionList.title: Comparator vs Comparable
options: Comparable defines a single natural ordering; Comparator allows multiple sort orders without modifying the class
Comparator must be implemented inside the class; Comparable is external
Comparable works only with Collections; Comparator works only with Arrays
They are identical — no practical difference between them
questionList.answer: Comparable defines a single natural ordering; Comparator allows multiple sort orders without modifying the class

questionList.title: ExecutorService: submit vs execute
options: submit() returns a Future for tracking result/exception; execute() returns void
execute() is asynchronous; submit() is synchronous
submit() creates a new thread; execute() reuses threads
There is no difference — they are aliases
questionList.answer: submit() returns a Future for tracking result/exception; execute() returns void

questionList.title: ConcurrentHashMap vs Hashtable
options: ConcurrentHashMap uses lock striping for better concurrency; Hashtable locks the entire map

questionList.title: Generics: Type Erasure
questionList.prompt: In Java, generics are implemented through ___ which means the generic type information is removed at ___. This is why `List<String>` and `List<Integer>` are considered the same type at runtime — this is called a ___ type.
options: type erasure
compile time
runtime
raw
reified
polymorphic
questionList.answer: type erasure, compile time, raw

questionList.title: Thread States: BLOCKED vs WAITING
options: WAITING — releases the lock and waits for notify()
BLOCKED — holds the lock while waiting
TIMED_WAITING — wait() has an implicit timeout
RUNNABLE — wait() is non-blocking
questionList.answer: WAITING — releases the lock and waits for notify()

questionList.title: Immutable Class Design
options: The class must be abstract — immutable classes must be abstract by design
All fields must be private and final
No setter methods should be provided
Mutable fields must be defensively copied in constructor and getter
questionList.answer: The class must be abstract — immutable classes must be abstract by design

questionList.title: Java Memory Model & Synchronization
questionList.prompt: Which statements about Java's memory model are correct? (Select all that apply)
options: The synchronized keyword provides both mutual exclusion and visibility guarantees
A thread entering a synchronized block always sees the latest values of all shared variables
The volatile keyword ensures atomicity for compound operations like i++
The happens-before relationship guarantees changes in one synchronized block are visible to the next thread on the same lock
Static synchronized methods lock on the Class object, not the instance
questionList.answer: The synchronized keyword provides both mutual exclusion and visibility guarantees, A thread entering a synchronized block always sees the latest values of all shared variables, The happens-before relationship guarantees changes in one synchronized block are visible to the next thread on the same lock, Static synchronized methods lock on the Class object, not the instance

questionList.title: Thread-Safe Singleton Patterns
options: A: Eager Initialization (thread-safe by class loading)
B: Double-Checked Locking with volatile
C: Enum-based (thread-safe by JVM guarantee)
D: Lazy without synchronization
questionList.answer: A: Eager Initialization (thread-safe by class loading), B: Double-Checked Locking with volatile, C: Enum-based (thread-safe by JVM guarantee)

questionList.title: Reverse a Linked List
Monolith to Microservices Migration Strategy
questionList.prompt:
## Monolith to Microservices Migration

Describe your approach for migrating a large monolithic Java app to microservices. Cover:

1. How to identify service boundaries
2. Inter-service communication patterns (sync vs async)
3. Handling distributed transactions
4. Monitoring and observability approach

Provide concrete examples for each point.
questionList.answer: 1. DDD bounded contexts, strangler fig pattern. 2. REST/gRPC for sync, Kafka for async events, CQRS. 3. Saga pattern with compensating transactions, outbox pattern for reliable messaging. 4. Prometheus+Grafana for metrics, Jaeger for tracing, ELK for logging.

questionList.title: Find First Non-Repeating Character
questionList.prompt:
## Find the First Non-Repeating Character in a String

Given a string, find the first character that appears only once. Return that character, or '_' if no unique character exists.

```java
public class CharacterFinder {
    public static char firstUnique(String s) {
        // Your code here
    }
}
```

**Examples:**
```
Input: "swiss"
Output: 'w' (s appears twice, w appears once first)

Input: "aabbcc"
Output: '_'

Input: "leetcode"
Output: 'l'
```

**Constraints:**
- String length: 1 to 10^5
- Characters: lowercase English letters only
- Time: O(n), Space: O(1) [26 letters]
